what_its_for: Glycopyrronium is used for several different conditions depending on the form your doctor prescribed. It can help open up your airways if you have chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), making it easier to breathe. It can also reduce drooling in children with certain nerve or muscle conditions, decrease stomach acid and spasms, or reduce sweating when used as a medicated cloth wipe applied to the skin.
how_to_take: How you take this medicine depends on the form prescribed. If you have an inhaler, breathe it in deeply through your mouth as instructed. If it is a liquid to swallow, use the measuring tool that came with it and take it on an empty stomach at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. If it is a skin wipe (cloth), use it on your underarms, hands, or feet and let the area dry before touching anything or putting on clothes. Always follow the specific instructions your doctor or pharmacist gave you.
dosing: Your dose depends on the form and what condition is being treated. For COPD inhalers, the usual dose is one inhalation once or twice a day. For the liquid used for drooling in children, the dose is based on body weight and given up to 3 times a day. For skin wipes for sweating, use one wipe on each underarm once a day. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed and never take more than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store glycopyrronium at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the inhaler dry and store it in its pouch until you are ready to use it. Keep the liquid medicine tightly closed. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze the liquid form.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the skin wipe in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on broken skin, as it can cause irritation. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase dizziness. Be careful in hot weather or during heavy exercise because this medicine can make it harder for your body to sweat and cool down, raising your risk of overheating. Avoid driving or using machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it may cause blurred vision or dizziness. Avoid antacids within 1 hour of taking the liquid form, as they can reduce how well it works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience difficulty urinating or no urination at all, severe constipation or stomach pain, a fast or irregular heartbeat, confusion or unusual behavior, high body temperature or hot dry skin with no sweating, eye pain or sudden vision changes, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your breathing symptoms do not improve or get worse when using the inhaler form.
when_it_works: For COPD, you should notice easier breathing within 5 minutes of using the inhaler, and its full effect lasts up to 12 to 24 hours. For drooling, it may take a few days to a week to see a noticeable reduction. For sweating with the skin wipe, you may notice less sweating within 1 week of daily use. Take this medicine every day as prescribed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like confusion, dizziness, constipation, and urinary problems, so use with extra caution. Children using the liquid form for drooling should be monitored closely for side effects, especially constipation and urinary retention. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medicine, as safety has not been fully established. People with glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, bladder problems, or kidney or liver disease should talk to their doctor before using this medicine, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed.
